title: Blackjack
tagline: A playable blackjack game, shown end-to-end in a full play-through video.
summary: Blackjack is a card game project by Michael Lizzio, presented on the legacy portfolio as a screenshot gallery plus a video walkthrough. The page carries five interface screenshots and one video that, in the author's words, "shows a full play through of the game and all of its features." The write-up itself was never finished: the entire project story is the placeholder line "blackjack!!!", and the gallery heading still reads "Cryptogram Examples" from the page it was copied from. A porter should treat this as a stub that needs real prose written by the author before it can ship.

hero.alt: Cover image for the Blackjack project, listed as its cover art in the stale data/projects copy.json; the live homepage data file does not reference it.

sections.heading: Cryptogram Examples
body: The legacy page opens with a large display image and a row of five clickable thumbnails; clicking a thumbnail swaps it into the big display slot above. The section heading is literally "Cryptogram Examples" in the source, which is a copy-paste leftover from the Cryptogram Solver page — these are Blackjack screenshots, not cryptograms. A commented-out subheading reading "[Unsolved, Solved]" sits just above it, another leftover from the same page.

notes:
STUB PAGE — this is the thinnest project write-up on the site. The entire project story is the single placeholder line "blackjack!!!"; there is no description of how the game works, what language or libraries it uses, when it was built, or its status. tech, year, status, and links are therefore all empty/null: nothing on the page states any of them, and inventing them would violate the extraction rules. NOT ON THE HOMEPAGE. data/projects.json (the live file the homepage fetches) contains only "foosball" and "cryptogram" — Blackjack is absent, so the legacy homepage never linked to this page. Blackjack DOES appear in the stale duplicate data/projects copy.json, with title "BLACKJACK" (all caps), an empty description, cover image "blackjack_cover.png", and page "blackjack". That copy file also lists alarm_system, wordle_solver, and cyber_TTM — and note that its cyber_TTM entry has a bug: its "page" value is "blackjack", so restoring that file verbatim would send Cybersecurity File Editor visitors to the Blackjack page. Decide deliberately whether Blackjack is restored to the project grid. HERO CHOICE. The page's own large display image is screen_0.png; data/project_images/blackjack/blackjack_cover.png is the designated cover art from the copy JSON and is not referenced by any HTML in the repo. I used the cover as "hero" and kept screen_0.png first in the gallery, matching its role as the default big image. Swap them if the rebuild prefers the in-page hero. HEADING IS WRONG IN THE SOURCE. The gallery heading literally reads "Cryptogram Examples" — copied from project_pages/cryptogram and never updated. A commented-out "

[Unsolved, Solved]

" above it is from the same page, and the video box carries id="webscraping-video" — a third leftover, shared verbatim with cryptogram.html, wordle_solver.html and cyber_TTM.html. Rename the heading to something like "Screenshots" or "Game Screens" in the rebuild; I kept the source heading verbatim so the discrepancy is visible. MEDIA PATHS ALL RESOLVE. Every src uses the "../../" prefix, which from project_pages/blackjack/ correctly resolves to the repo-relative paths above; all six referenced files are present in media-manifest.tsv. No broken media references on this page. Heads-up on weight: blackjack_show.mp4 is ~83 MB and blackjack_cover.png is ~2.1 MB — both want transcoding/compression and lazy loading in Next.js rather than a straight copy. CROSS-PAGE MEDIA REUSE. project_pages/alarm_system/alarm_system.html points its ENTIRE gallery at data/project_images/blackjack/* (screen_0 through screen_4) and also references data/project_images/blackjack/hardware.png, hardware_components.png, main_screen.png, and settings_screen.png — none of which exist in the manifest. Those four are broken references on the Alarm System page, not this one, but they explain why Blackjack's screenshots may look out of place there. Do not let the Alarm System port silently inherit Blackjack's images. BROKEN SCRIPT REFERENCE. blackjack.html loads
